section.content: The application discloses a lithium ion battery diaphragm and a lithium ion battery, wherein the lithium ion battery diaphragm comprises a base film, at least one surface of the base film is provided with a functional coating, the functional coating contains NTC material particles and ceramic particles, the mass content of the NTC material particles is 30-80 wt% based on the functional coating, the base film is a base film with low rupture temperature, and the rupture temperature of the base film is not higher than 180 ℃. The application uses the base film with low rupture temperature and negative temperature coefficient material to combine and match, so that in the early stage of thermal safety test (before failure), the base film with low rupture temperature forms a micro short circuit point, and then the NTC material and ceramic particle combined coating realizes large-area micro self-discharge, and the base film with low rupture temperature and NTC material in a certain range cooperate to realize controllable self-discharge rate, thereby being beneficial to quickly reducing the SOC of the battery and improving the thermal safety performance of the battery.

本申请公开了一种锂离子电池隔膜、锂离子电池，所述锂离子电池隔膜包括基膜，所述基膜的至少一表面设置有功能性涂层，所述功能性涂层含有NTC材料颗粒和陶瓷颗粒，以所述功能性涂层为基准，所述NTC材料颗粒的质量含量为30～80wt％，所述基膜为低破膜温度的基膜，所述基膜的破膜温度不高于180℃。本申请通过使用低破膜温度的基膜与负温度系数材料组合搭配使用，以使在热安全测试的前期(失效前)，由低破膜温度的基膜形成微短路点，再由NTC材料与陶瓷颗粒组合涂层实现大面积的微小自放电，通过低破膜温度的基膜与一定范围内的NTC材料的协同，可实现可控的自放电速率，有利于快速降低电池SOC，提升电池的热安全性能。

Lithium ion battery diaphragm and lithium ion batteryTechnical Field

The application relates to the technical field of lithium ion batteries, in particular to a lithium ion battery diaphragm and a lithium ion battery.

Background

Currently, in order to pursue a battery with high energy density, a high-voltage system cathode lithium cobalt oxide is generally used, and in a fully charged state, the lithium cobalt oxide of the cathode has a large lithium removal amount, the structure is unstable, the cathode side has strong oxidizing property, and an electrolyte in a fast charging system is generally used as an electrolyte with low viscosity and high dielectric constant, and the boiling point flash point of the electrolyte is also lower, so that a higher requirement is placed on the thermal safety performance of the battery.

In order to improve the thermal safety performance of the battery, the prior art means include cathode primer coating (STS technology) and anode ceramic coating (CCA technology), which can increase the thickness of the battery cell to reduce the energy density of the battery cell, and can affect the quick charge performance of the battery in either STS technology or CCA technology.

Disclosure of Invention

In view of the above, the present application provides a lithium ion battery separator and a lithium ion battery, which can improve the thermal safety performance of the battery and also can give consideration to the energy density and the rate capability of the battery.

In a first aspect, the application provides a lithium ion battery diaphragm, which comprises a base film, wherein at least one surface of the base film is provided with a functional coating, the functional coating contains NTC material particles and ceramic particles, the mass content of the NTC material particles is 30-80 wt% based on the functional coating, the base film is a base film with low rupture temperature, and the rupture temperature of the base film is not higher than 180 ℃. Preferably, the rupture temperature of the base film is 135-180 ℃.

When lithium cobaltate (Li xCoO2) is in high lithium removal amount (0.5 > x > 0.45) and charging voltage is about 4.2V, the lithium cobaltate is converted from a hexagonal system H-2 into a monoclinic system M, the monoclinic system M belongs to a P12/M1 space group, the process is accompanied by irregular change of unit cell parameters, for example, as shown in figure 1, when the lithium cobaltate is in an O1 phase from an H1-3 phase, a discharge platform exists, the lithium cobaltate in the O1 phase is unstable at high temperature (in a thermal safety test environment), the reason of the phenomenon is probably that the space rule of lithium ions and lithium vacancies changes, the rule of ordered-disordered-ordered change is presented, the thermal stability of the lithium cobaltate material in a high lithium removal state is poor, thermal runaway is easy to cause, and the improvement of the safety performance of a battery is unfavorable. In order to improve the safety performance of the battery, the application selects the base film with the rupture temperature of 135-180 ℃ and combines the functional coating containing a proper amount of NTC material particles and ceramic particles, and through the cooperation of the base film with the low rupture temperature and the functional coating, the self-discharge of the battery core can be promoted, so that lithium ions are back-intercalated into Li XCoO2 (X is less than 0.1) which is extremely deficient in lithium, thereby ensuring the structure to be stable, accelerating the self-discharge of the battery at high temperature in the early stage of the thermal safety test, being beneficial to the improvement of the thermal stability of battery anode materials, especially high-voltage lithium cobalt oxide, and being capable of remarkably improving the thermal safety test passing rate of the battery; the early stage of the thermal safety test is a period of adding the two stages, namely, the stage of raising the temperature from the room temperature to the preset test temperature and the stage of keeping the temperature at the preset test temperature to the first third of the total test period.

If the ratio of the NTC material particles is too small (< 30%), the self-discharge rate will be too small, and the rapid discharge in the early stage of the thermal safety test will not be realized, and if the ratio of the NTC material particles is too high (> 80%), on the one hand, the heat generation of the battery in the self-discharge process is uncontrollable, which is unfavorable for the improvement of the thermal safety performance, on the other hand, the ratio of the ceramic particles will necessarily be too low, at this time, the lack of the ceramic particles plays a supporting and blocking role, and at high temperature (above 120 ℃, hereinafter, the high temperature is above 120 ℃), the ceramic particles are difficult to play a "skeleton" role to support the base film, which in turn leads to the excessive self-discharge rate, the uncontrollability of the self-discharge rate and even the possibility of thermal runaway.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles are selected from at least one of metal oxide particles having a spinel structure or metal oxide particles having a perovskite structure. The negative temperature coefficient inorganic material is made of metal oxides such as manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper and the like as main materials by adopting a ceramic process, and has semiconductor properties. When the temperature is low (less than or equal to 100 ℃), the number of carriers (electrons and holes) of the metal oxide particles is small, so that the resistance value is high, but as the temperature is increased (more than 100 ℃), the number of carriers is increased, the resistance value is reduced, and when the temperature is increased to more than 120 ℃, the cathode and anode are conducted, so that the overall potential of the battery core is reduced.

The metal oxide particles with spinel structure or the metal oxide particles with perovskite structure are more favorable for being matched with the base film with low rupture temperature to generate local micro short circuit points at high temperature so as to realize controllable self-discharge and be favorable for improving the thermal safety performance of the battery. The perovskite-type NTC material mainly comprises a Re (Cr, mn) O 3 system, a BaTiO 3 system and the like, and the type can exert thermal properties, wherein the thermal properties refer to that the material keeps insulation in a formation and storage environment, but the material is converted into a semiconductor and a conductor from an insulator along with the rise of temperature (higher than 100 ℃), so that the conduction of a cathode and an anode is realized, and the self discharge at high temperature is realized. For example, the YCrO 3 material with a typical rare earth perovskite structure has loose and porous structure after high-temperature sintering, has poor ageing resistance, is Y1-xCaxCrO3、YCr1-xMnxO3、YCo1-xMnxO3、Y0.9Ca0.1Cr1-xMnxO3 after doping modification and the like, has adjustable thermosensitive property in a certain range, and has improved compactness and pore structure after sintering to a certain extent.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles are metal oxide particles having a spinel structure, wherein a Mn spinel structure is further preferred, the Mn spinel structure NTC material particles contain Mn element, O element, and T element, and the T element is at least one selected from Ni element, fe element, cu element, co element, and Zn element, and in the Mn spinel structure NTC material particles, the molar amount of the Mn element is denoted as n Mn, and the molar amount of the T element is denoted as n T, where: n Mn/nT is more than or equal to 0.76 and less than or equal to 6.5. The NTC material of Mn series spinel structure doped with different metal ions has different thermal properties, wherein the NTC material of Mn series spinel structure doped with quaternary or more metal elements has optimal thermal properties, which is more beneficial to realizing controllable self-discharge in cooperation with a base film with low rupture temperature. For example, cu 0.2Ni0.5Zn1.0Mn1.3O4, the thermal sensitive ceramic has small particle size and large specific surface area, and the thermal sensitive property of the material is controllable at-60-300 ℃. The conduction mechanism of the spinel structure material is that metal cations have multiple valence states, the valence-changing metals occupy different crystallographic positions, and electrons can generate jumping phenomenon among ions in different valence states. The electron jump phenomenon is influenced by external conditions, and in the NTC material of the spinel structure material, the electron jump is aggravated along with the temperature rise, so that the controllable self-discharge can be generated at high temperature by matching with a base film with low film rupture temperature.

In some embodiments, in the functional coating, the NTC material particles have a mass content of 50 to 80wt%, the ceramic particles have a mass content ranging from 15 to 45wt%, and the remaining components are a dispersant, a binder, and a wetting agent. At this time, a proper self-discharge rate can be achieved at a high temperature, so that the voltage is more favorable for rapid voltage drop in the early stage of thermal safety test, thermal safety can be considered, and the battery can pass the thermal box test more favorably.

In some embodiments, the lithium ion battery separator has a self-discharge rate of 120 to 260mV/h at ambient temperatures above 120 ℃. Preferably, the self-discharge rate of the lithium ion battery diaphragm at the ambient temperature above 120 ℃ is 180-220 mV/h.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles have an average particle size, denoted D 1, and the ceramic particles have an average particle size, denoted D 2, that satisfies the following: d 1/D2 is more than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to 25. At this time, the particle size ratio of NTC material particles is further limited, so that the thermal shrinkage of the base film can be better restrained, the coating is more compact, and the improvement of quick charge performance is facilitated. Preferably, D 1 is 0.5 to 2 μm and D 2 is 0.1 to 0.5 μm. More preferably, D 1 is 0.5 to 1.5 μm and D 2 is 0.3 to 0.5 μm.

In some embodiments, the base film has a thickness of 3 to 6 μm. At this time, on the one hand, the base film with proper thickness is favorable to realizing local rupture of membranes under the high temperature, more is favorable to cooperating with functional coating, realizes controllable self-discharge, and on the other hand, the base film with proper thickness is favorable to promoting battery volume energy density.

In some embodiments, the functional coating has a thickness of 2 to 8 μm. At this time, the combination of the proper coating thickness and the proper base film thickness is more beneficial to the improvement of the energy density of the battery, and can give consideration to the heat shrinkage performance of the diaphragm and better realize the function of reducing the potential of the NTC material.

In a second aspect, the application provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive electrode plate, a negative electrode plate, a diaphragm and electrolyte, wherein the diaphragm is arranged between the positive electrode plate and the negative electrode plate, the diaphragm is any one of the lithium ion battery diaphragms, and the positive electrode plate contains a lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode material.

The technical scheme provided by the embodiments of the application has the beneficial effects that at least: the lithium ion battery diaphragm can fundamentally improve the thermal safety of a battery core, and the base film with low rupture temperature and the negative temperature coefficient material are combined and matched for use, so that a micro short circuit point is formed by the base film with low rupture temperature in the early stage of thermal safety test (before failure), and then the NTC material and ceramic particle combined coating realizes large-area micro self discharge, thereby reducing the integral voltage of the battery core, promoting full-state anode delithiation and lithium ion back-intercalation to a cathode, improving the structural stability of the cathode, reducing the oxidization of the cathode, and reducing the side reaction heat generation of a cathode oxidation electrolyte. Through the cooperation of the base film with low rupture temperature and a proper amount of NTC material, controllable self-discharge rate can be realized, so that the battery core can form high-temperature self-discharge of the whole surface of the pole piece in the early stage of testing, the SOC of the battery to be tested is reduced, and the battery with low SOC is more beneficial to passing a thermal safety test.

In order to more clearly illustrate the embodiments of the application or the technical solutions in the prior art, the drawings that are necessary for the description of the embodiments or the prior art will be briefly described, it being obvious that the drawings in the following description are only some embodiments of the application and that other drawings may be obtained from them without inventive effort for a person skilled in the art.

Detailed Description

The present application will be described in further detail with reference to the drawings, examples and comparative examples, in order to make the objects, technical solutions and advantages of the present application more apparent. It should be understood that the specific embodiments described herein are for purposes of illustration only and are not intended to limit the scope of the application.

Lithium ion battery

The embodiment of the application provides a lithium ion battery, which comprises a positive pole piece, a negative pole piece, a diaphragm and electrolyte.

Diaphragm

The diaphragm comprises a base film, wherein at least one surface of the base film is provided with a functional coating, the functional coating contains NTC material particles and ceramic particles, the mass content of the NTC material particles is 30-80 wt% based on the functional coating, the base film is a base film with low rupture temperature, and the rupture temperature of the base film is not higher than 180 ℃. The schematic structure of the diaphragm is shown in fig. 2, the diaphragm is broken in a base film with low rupture temperature under a heated environment, the ceramic layer is isolated between the rupture and the conducted cathode and anode, the NTC material exerts adjustable self-discharge to reduce the cathode potential, the lithium cobaltate phase change of a used 4.45V/4.48V/4.50V system is converted from an unstable H1-3 phase to a relatively stable monoclinic system M, the corresponding voltage is 4.4V, and the corresponding high-temperature self-discharge rate is 120-260 mV/H.

Illustratively, the mass content of the NTC material particles is 30wt%, 40wt%, 50wt%, 60wt%, 70wt%, 80wt% or a range of any two of the above values.

Illustratively, the base film has a rupture temperature of 135 ℃, 140 ℃, 145 ℃, 150 ℃, 155 ℃, 160 ℃, 165 ℃, 170 ℃, 175 ℃, 180 ℃, or a range of any two values described above.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles are selected from at least one of metal oxide particles having a spinel structure or metal oxide particles having a perovskite structure.

Specifically, in some examples, the NTC material particles are metal oxide particles having a spinel structure, in other examples, the NTC material particles are metal oxide particles having a perovskite structure, or in other examples, the NTC material particles include metal oxide particles having a spinel structure, and further include metal oxide particles having a perovskite structure.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles have an average particle size, denoted D 1, and the ceramic particles have an average particle size, denoted D 2, that satisfies the following: d 1/D2 is more than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to 25.

Illustratively, the ratio of D 1/D2 is 1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or a range of any two of the values recited above.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles are spinel-structured metal oxide particles, and the spinel-structured metal oxide particles contain Mn element, O element, and optionally T element, where the T element is at least one selected from Ni element, fe element, cu element, or Zn element, and in the spinel-structured metal oxide particles, the molar amount of the Mn element is denoted as n Mn, and the molar amount of the T element is denoted as n T, where: n Mn/nT is more than or equal to 0.76 and less than or equal to 6.5.

Specifically, in some examples, the metal oxide particles having a spinel structure contain Mn element and O element, and in other examples, the metal oxide particles having a spinel structure contain T element in addition to Mn element and O element.

Illustratively, the ratio of n Mn/nT is 0.76, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5, 6.0, 6.5, or a range of any two of the values recited above.

In some embodiments, in the functional coating, the NTC material particles have a mass content of 50 to 80wt%, the ceramic particles have a mass content ranging from 15 to 45wt%, and the remaining components are a dispersant, a binder, and a wetting agent.

The binder is selected from at least one of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), or polyacrylic acid (PAA).

The dispersing agent is at least one selected from Sodium Polyacrylate (SPA) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC).

The wetting agent is at least one selected from polyoxyethylene alkylphenol ether, polyoxyethylene fatty alcohol ether or polyoxyethylene polyoxypropylene block ester.

Illustratively, the mass content of the NTC material particles is 50wt%, 60wt%, 70wt%, 80wt% or a range of any two values of the above.

Illustratively, the ceramic particles have a mass content of 15wt%, 20wt%, 25wt%, 30wt%, 35wt%, 40wt%, 45wt%, or a range of any two of the above values.

In some embodiments, the NTC material particles have an average particle size D 1 of 0.5-2 μm. Preferably, the NTC material particles have an average particle diameter D 1 of 0.5-1.5 μm.

Illustratively, the NTC material particles have an average particle size D 1 of 0.5 μm, 0.6 μm, 0.7 μm, 0.8 μm, 0.9 μm, 1 μm, 1.3 μm, 1.5 μm, 1.8 μm, 2 μm, or a range of any two values described above.

In some embodiments, the ceramic particles have an average particle size D 2 of 0.1 to 0.5 μm. Preferably, the ceramic particles have an average particle diameter D 2 of 0.3 to 0.5. Mu.m.

Illustratively, the ceramic particles have an average particle size D 2 of 0.1 μm, 0.2 μm, 0.3 μm, 0.4 μm, 0.5 μm, or a range of any two values recited above.

In some embodiments, the lithium ion battery separator has a self-discharge rate of 120 to 260mV/h at ambient temperatures above 120 ℃. Preferably, the self-discharge rate of the lithium ion battery diaphragm at the ambient temperature above 120 ℃ is 180-220 mV/h.

Illustratively, the lithium ion battery separator has a self-discharge rate of 120mV/h, 140mV/h, 160mV/h, 180mV/h, 190mV/h, 200mV/h, 210mV/h, 220mV/h, 240mV/h, 260mV/h, or a range of any two of the foregoing values at ambient temperatures above 120 ℃.

In some embodiments, the base film has a thickness of 3 to 6 μm.

Illustratively, the low rupture base membrane has a thickness of 3 μm, 3.5 μm, 4 μm, 4.5 μm, 5 μm, 5.5 μm, 6 μm, or a range of any two values recited above.

In some embodiments, the functional coating has a thickness of 2 to 8 μm.

Illustratively, the functional coating has a thickness of 2 μm, 3 μm, 4 μm, 5 μm, 6 μm, 7 μm, 8 μm or a range of any two values recited above.

An exemplary preparation method of the base film with low rupture temperature comprises the following steps: the components with low rupture of membranes are mixed in the preparation raw materials of the base membrane. For example, PE with a certain mass ratio of 0-20% is doped into the PP film, so that the film breaking temperature of the PP film can be reduced integrally, and meanwhile, the tensile property can be improved; for PE base film, the molecular weight of polyethylene can be regulated to be 30-200 ten thousand, the molecular weight distribution is more preferably 40-60 ten thousand for ensuring the processing performance and mechanical property, the PDI=M W/Mn=6-8, the film breaking temperature of the base film can be regulated to be 135-180 ℃, and the parameter for representing the film breaking temperature is film breaking temperature T, which can be actually measured. The specific operation process of the base film with low film breaking temperature can refer to the conventional technical means in the prior art, and the application is not repeated.

And coating the slurry on one side or two sides of the base film, and after coating a ceramic layer (functional coating), normally coating an adhesive layer on the ceramic layer to obtain the lithium ion battery diaphragm.

Others

Positive electrode plate

The lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode comprises a positive electrode current collector and a positive electrode active material layer arranged on at least one surface of the positive electrode current collector, wherein the positive electrode active material layer optionally contains lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode material.

For example, a metal foil or a porous metal plate, for example, a foil or a porous plate of a metal such as aluminum, copper, nickel, titanium, or iron, or an alloy thereof, such as Al (aluminum) foil, may be used as the positive electrode current collector.

The positive electrode sheet may be prepared according to a conventional method in the art.

Negative pole piece

The negative electrode active layer comprises a negative electrode current collector and a negative electrode active layer arranged on the surface of the negative electrode current collector, wherein the negative electrode active layer comprises a negative electrode active material. The thickness of the anode active layer is not particularly limited as long as the object of the present application can be achieved, for example, the anode active layer has a thickness of 30 μm to 120 μm. In some embodiments, the anode active material may include at least one of a carbon material or a silicon-based material. In some embodiments, the carbon material includes, but is not limited to, at least one of natural graphite, artificial graphite, mesophase micro carbon spheres, hard carbon, or soft carbon. In some embodiments, the silicon-based material includes, but is not limited to, at least one of silicon, a silicon oxygen composite, or a silicon carbon composite. The negative electrode current collector of the present application is not particularly limited as long as the object of the present application can be achieved, and for example, copper foil, copper alloy foil, nickel foil, stainless steel foil, titanium foil, foam nickel, foam copper, or a composite current collector (for example, a composite current collector in which a metal layer is provided on the surface of a polymer layer) may be included. The thickness of the negative electrode current collector is not particularly limited as long as the object of the present application can be achieved, for example, the thickness of the negative electrode current collector is 5 μm to 12 μm. The anode active layer may further include a binder and a thickener, and the present application is not particularly limited in kind as long as the object of the present application can be achieved. For example, the binder may include, but is not limited to, at least one of polyvinyl alcohol, polyvinyl chloride, carboxylated polyvinyl chloride, polyvinyl fluoride, polyvinyl pyrrolidone, polyurethane, polytetrafluoroethylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, styrene-butadiene rubber, or acrylated styrene-butadiene rubber; the thickener may include, but is not limited to, at least one of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or lithium carboxymethyl cellulose. The anode active layer may further include a conductive agent, and the present application is not particularly limited in kind as long as the object of the present application can be achieved. For example, the conductive agent may include, but is not limited to, at least one of conductive carbon black, carbon Nanotubes (CNTs), carbon fibers, ketjen black, graphene, metallic materials, or conductive polymers. The mass ratio of the anode active material, the conductive agent, the binder and the thickener in the anode active layer is not particularly limited in the present application, and may be selected by those skilled in the art according to actual needs as long as the object of the present application can be achieved. Optionally, the negative electrode tab may further comprise a conductive layer located between the negative electrode current collector and the negative electrode active layer. The composition of the conductive layer is not particularly limited in the present application, and may be a conductive layer commonly used in the art. For example, the conductive layer includes a conductive agent and a binder. The conductive agent and the binder in the conductive layer are not particularly limited in the present application, and may be at least one of the conductive agent and the binder in the above-described anode active layer, for example.

Electrolyte solution

Comprises an organic solvent and lithium salt; the organic solvent comprises a carbonate solvent, a carboxylate solvent or a combination thereof; wherein the carbonate solvent comprises at least one of diethyl carbonate (DEC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), dipropyl carbonate (DPC), methylpropyl carbonate (MPC), ethylpropyl carbonate (EPC), methylethyl carbonate (EMC), ethylene Carbonate (EC), propylene Carbonate (PC) or Butylene Carbonate (BC). The carboxylic acid ester solvent comprises at least one of ethyl formate, methyl acetate, ethyl acetate, propyl acetate, methyl propionate, ethyl propionate, propyl propionate, butyl butyrate, ethyl difluoroacetate, ethyl trifluoroacetate or methyl trifluoropropionate. The lithium salt includes at least one of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF 6), lithium bis (oxalato) borate (LiB (C 2O4)2, liBOB), lithium difluoro (LiBF 2(C2O4), lithium tetrafluoroborate (LiBF 4), lithium bis (fluorosulfonyl) imide salt (LiFSI), or lithium bis (trifluoromethylsulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI). The electrolyte may further include an electrolyte additive, which may include, but is not limited to, at least one of fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), ethylene carbonate (VC), or 1, 3-Propane Sultone (PS).

Hereinafter, embodiments of the present application will be described in more detail with reference to examples and comparative examples. Unless otherwise indicated, the parts, percentages and ratios listed below are based on weight, and the starting materials used are either commercially available or synthetically obtained according to conventional methods.

Example 1

Preparation of lithium ion battery separator

A base film with a film breaking temperature of 135 ℃ is selected, one side of the base film is coated with coating slurry, the coating slurry contains NTC material particles, ceramic particles and other components, the other components comprise dispersing agent (SPA), binder (PVDF) and wetting agent (polyoxyethylene alkylphenol ether), and specific parameters are shown in Table 1. An SEM image of the NTC material particles in example 1 is shown in fig. 3, and a temperature resistance curve thereof is shown in fig. 4.

As can be seen from fig. 3, the NTC material particles are spinel structures;

as can be seen from fig. 4, the NTC material particles gradually decrease in their resistivity with increasing temperature over a certain temperature range. Wherein, the resistance change rate refers to the change difference value of the resistance when the temperature is changed by 1 ℃.

Examples 2 to 5 compared with example 1, except that examples 2 to 5 further adjust the content of NTC material particles and the content of ceramic particles, see table 1 in particular.

Example 6 the difference compared to example 1 is that example 6 uses a base film with a different rupture temperature, see in particular table 1.

Examples 7 and 8 are selected from NTC material particles different from examples 1 to 6, wherein example 7 is also spinel-structured manganese-based quaternary NTC particles, but the molar ratio of the elements thereof is not within the proper range of the present application, and example 8 is spinel-structured manganese-based non-quaternary NTC particles, see in particular table 1.

Examples 9 to 10 are different from example 1 in that example 9 uses NTC particles having a perovskite structure and example 10 uses NTC particles having a non-perovskite structure and also a non-spinel structure, as shown in table 1.

Example 11 differs from example 1 in that the content of ceramic particles in example 11 is not in a suitable range, specifically as shown in table 1.

Example 12 in comparison with example 1, the difference in example 12 is that a coating paste is applied to both sides of a base film.

Example 13 differs from example 1 in that the rupture temperature of the base film used in example 13 is 130 ℃.

Comparative examples 1 to 3 are different from example 1 in that comparative examples 1 and 2 contain only one of NTC material particles and ceramic particles, and the remaining content is the other component, and comparative example 3 contains NTC material particles and ceramic particles in an unsuitable range, specifically, see table 1.

Examples 14 to 20 compared with example 4, except that examples 14 to 20 further adjust the average particle diameter D 1 of the NTC material particles and the average particle diameter D 2 of the ceramic particles, see table 2 in particular.

Examples 21 to 23 differ from example 17 in that examples 21 to 23 vary the base film thickness and the coating thickness, as shown in table 2.

Preparation of positive electrode plate

Adding an anode active material, namely LiCoO 2 (4.5V), conductive carbon black Super-P and a binder PVDF into an N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) solvent system according to the weight ratio of 97.6:1.3:1.1, and fully stirring by a vacuum stirrer to obtain anode slurry; and coating the positive electrode slurry on two surfaces of a 9 mu m Al foil substrate, wherein the coating weight is 280mg, and drying, cold pressing, slitting and cutting are sequentially carried out to obtain a positive electrode plate, and the thickness of the positive electrode plate after cold pressing is 95 mu m.

Preparation of negative electrode plate

The negative electrode graphite active material-silicon oxide material (graphite and silicon-based material silicon oxide SiO X are mixed according to the mass ratio of 90 percent to 10 percent), thickener sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and binder styrene butadiene rubber according to the mass ratio of 96:2:2, dissolving in water, fully stirring and uniformly mixing to obtain the negative electrode slurry, wherein the average particle size of the silicon-based material is 7 mu m. The negative electrode slurry is uniformly coated on a negative electrode current collector copper foil with the thickness of 12 mu m, and the negative electrode current collector copper foil is dried at 120 ℃ to obtain a negative electrode plate with a negative electrode active material layer coated on one side. And repeating the steps on the other surface of the copper foil to obtain the negative electrode plate with the negative electrode active material layer coated on both sides, and compacting and cutting to obtain the negative electrode plate.

Preparation of electrolyte

In a dry argon atmosphere glove box, uniformly mixing Ethylene Carbonate (EC), ethylmethyl carbonate (EMC) and diethyl carbonate (DEC) according to the mass ratio of EC to DEC=30:50:20, adding lithium salt LiPF 6, and uniformly mixing to obtain an electrolyte, wherein the mass percentage of LiPF 6 is 12.5% based on the mass of the electrolyte. Wherein the viscosity of the electrolyte is 3-6 mpa.s.

Preparation of lithium ion batteries

And sequentially stacking the positive electrode plate, the lithium ion battery diaphragm and the negative electrode plate, wherein the lithium ion battery diaphragm is positioned between the positive electrode plate and the negative electrode plate to play a role in isolation, then winding the lithium ion battery diaphragm into a bare cell, filling the bare cell into an aluminum plastic film, injecting electrolyte and sealing, and then performing procedures such as standing, formation, shaping and the like to obtain the lithium ion battery. Wherein the formation process comprises the following steps: at 45 ℃, the first charge and discharge are carried out, and the flow is as follows: firstly, constant current charging is carried out for 10min at the rate of 0.1C, then constant current charging is carried out to the specified voltage of 4.6V at the rate of 0.5C, then constant voltage charging is carried out to the current of less than or equal to 0.05C, and then constant current discharging is carried out to 3.0V at the rate of 0.5C.

The testing method comprises the following steps:

(1) Hot box test

Step 1: charging the prepared battery to cut-off voltage of 4.5V at constant current of 0.5C, charging to cut-off current of 200mA at constant voltage, and standing for 5 minutes;

Step 2: attaching a temperature sensing wire to the fully charged battery, attaching the temperature sensing wire between two pole ears, connecting the two pole ears to monitor voltage, and vertically hanging the battery core in the box body;

Step 3: the box was warmed to 130℃at a warming rate of 5℃and held for 60min.

Evaluation criteria: the battery passes without ignition or explosion.

(2) Self discharge rate test

The voltage of the battery in the step 2 of the hot box test just before suspension is recorded as V 1, the temperature is raised to 130 ℃, and after the battery is kept for 30min, the voltage is recorded as V 2;

Self-discharge rate=2 (V 1-V2).

(3) Thermal shrinkage test

Cutting the prepared diaphragm into 72.5mm in MD and 54.2mm in TD, fixing four corners on paper sheets by using adhesive tapes, putting the sample into a baking oven at 130 ℃, baking for 1h, and taking out the test MD and TD lengths I 1、l2;

MD heat shrinkage= (72.5-I 1)/72.5;

TD heat shrinkage= (54.2-l 2)/54.2.

(4) Rate capability test

The lithium ion battery was left at 25 ℃ for 10min, then charged to 3V at a rate of 0.2C, left at 10min, then charged to 4.5V at a rate of 0.7C, charged at a constant voltage of 4.5V until the off-current was 0.05C, left at 10min, finally discharged to 3V at different rates, capacities of 0.7C, 1.1C, 2C, 3C rate discharge were tested, respectively, and capacity retention = discharge capacity at different rates/discharge capacity at 0.7C rate was calculated.
